svg.title: Harness inside the sandbox and harness outside the sandbox
svg.desc: The top panel places the harness, the model credential, and the tools in one machine. The bottom panel places the harness and the credential on one computer and the tools on another.
svg.text: The harness sits inside the sandbox
One machine. One lifetime. Codex on the web starts the harness binary in this room.
Harness process
Transcript of the login-form task
Credential that calls the model
The decision about the next step
All of this lives on the sandbox disk
and in the sandbox process list.
Tools
Read the login form
Write the test
Run pytest
A shell here can read the same
files the harness uses.
Recycling this machine ends the harness process. The wait while the model writes is billed as a full dev machine.
A second lock, such as Codex marking its own config read-only for the shell, is the extra machinery this layout needs.
A worker outside the room can still hold a channel. The loop process itself shares the room with the commands.
Replacing a wedged checkout replaces the clerk that remembers the task.
The harness sits outside the sandbox
Harness environment. This process stays up for the whole conversation.
Transcript, model credential, and the next step live here.
Laptop: your user session, the program you launched.
Cloud: the vendor's workflow service. Cursor runs the loop in Temporal, on its workers.
The sandbox can be destroyed and a new one attached. The session remains here.
You pay a trip for every tool call, and you pay to boot or restore the room.
tool request, with a call id
stdout, files changed
Sandbox environment. Replaceable. The login-form repo and the test secrets live here.
The shell, the file edits, and the tests run in this process.
Laptop: a rule around the shell hides the rest of the computer. Same machine
as the harness, and a narrower view of the disk and the network.
Cloud: a virtual machine you can throw away. A snapshot seeds the replacement.
The model credential stays in the harness environment above.
